title: Instructions for Capstone Project 1 - Online Resume
summary: Written brief for Capstone Project 1: build a plain-HTML online resume as a multi-page site, then publish it on GitHub Pages. There is no solution code or walkthrough; the work is meant to be the learner's own.

concepts.heading: Required page structure
points: Single entry file named index.html, starting with the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration.
A head containing a title element whose text is 'My Resume'.
The body holds the resume sections: summary or objective, education (degrees, schools, dates), work experience (titles, employers, dates, responsibilities), skills, and awards or certifications.
Section headings use heading elements; collections of items use ul or ol lists.
Include a profile photo with an image element.
Anchor tags link to additional pages (for example Hobbies and Contact), which makes the resume a multi-page site.
Finish with a footer element carrying the owner's name and any copyright or disclaimer text. The brief points to the MDN footer reference for details.

concepts.heading: Constraints and expectations
points: HTML only: no CSS or JavaScript, even if the learner already knows them. This keeps the project within scope.
Treat it like professional work: look up unfamiliar elements in MDN or search rather than expecting every answer in the course.
Open index.html in a browser to confirm it renders correctly.
Push the project to GitHub, publish via GitHub Pages, share the link in the course Q&A, and leave feedback on other students' sites.

concepts.heading: FAQ takeaways
points: Capstones can go in a portfolio or be shown in interviews, because they have no official solution, so the result is original work. Course projects with published solutions are easier to recognise as course material.
Getting stuck is the point: gaps found while building show which earlier lessons or docs to revisit, since watching videos alone rarely cements a skill.

task.name: Capstone 1: Online Resume
task.starting_point: Empty project; the learner creates index.html from scratch (no starter files, no goal image beyond a linked example site).
task.goal: A multi-page, HTML-only online resume published on GitHub Pages.
steps: Create index.html with the doctype and a head whose title is 'My Resume'.
Write the body sections: summary, education, work experience, skills, awards/certifications.
Use headings for section titles and ul/ol for lists.
Add a profile photo with an img element.
Create extra pages (e.g. hobbies.html, contact.html) and link them with anchor tags.
Add a footer with name and copyright text.
Open in a browser to check it.
Push to GitHub and enable GitHub Pages.
Post the link in the Q&A and comment on others' projects.
task.expected_result: A working HTML-only resume site, reachable via a GitHub Pages URL, with links between pages.

pitfalls: Using CSS or JS, which the brief excludes.
(Extra) Broken relative links or image paths when pages sit in different folders; revisit the file paths lesson.
(Extra) GitHub Pages expects the entry file to be named index.html in lowercase.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson for the capstone; s04-portfolio (4.3) is the closest project but is a guided one.
gaps_and_ideas: Add a 'Capstone 1: Online Resume' project lesson with a checklist of the required elements (doctype, title, headings, lists, img, anchors, footer).
Tasks: build index.html; add hobbies.html and contact.html with working links; add a footer; validate the page.
Starter idea: an empty folder with a requirements checklist the learner ticks off.
Interactive demo idea: a checklist that scans pasted HTML and ticks off which required elements are present.
